_doc: Lines everybody shares, picked by what they're doing and why they came (Conversation.life_line, RinkPeople small talk). Tokens on top of PEOPLE.md 6: {for} (who they came for), {they} {them} {their} (that person's pronouns), {kin} ("my son", "my granddaughter", "my friend"), {until} ("7", "7:30"), {doing}, {job}, {employer}, {boss}, {place}. A line whose token can't be filled is skipped.

parent: I'm here for {for}. {they_cap}'s in there till {until}, and then we have to find the other glove.
That's {kin} out there. Number something. I'll know when {they} score.
{for}'s got practice till {until}. I drive, I watch, I hold the coffee. That's the job.
Watching {for}. Well, watching the clock and then {for}.
{kin_cap} wanted to come early. Always wants to come early. Then it's forty minutes to tie the skates.
sibling: {for}'s playing. Mom said I had to come.
I'm waiting for {for}. It's taking forever.
My {kin_bare} is out there. Don't tell {them} I watched.
grandparent: I drove in to see {for}. {they_cap} doesn't know I'm here yet. I like to surprise {them}.
That's {kin} out there. I taught {their} father to skate on this ice, so you could say it runs in the family.
I never miss {for}. Well, I missed one in 2019. We don't talk about it.
friend: I'm waiting for {for}, {they}'s in there till {until}.
{for}'s my ride. So I'm here till {until}, apparently.
Here for {for}. We're getting fries after. If {they} ever come out.
Watching {for} practise. Somebody has to tell {them} the truth about that backhand.
partner: {for} plays. I watch. Then I hear about it all the way home.
I'm here for {for}. Moral support, mostly. And the canteen.
{for} said this one matters. They all matter, apparently.
date: We're on a date. Don't make it weird.
{for} talked me into skating. I talked {them} into the fries after.
First time on skates in ten years. {for} says it's like riding a bike. It is not like riding a bike.
scout: Just watching. Nice rink. Cold coffee.
I'm here to look at a couple of kids. Can't say which. Can say the number 14's skating is honest.
Professional interest. That's all I'm allowed to say, and I'm already saying too much.
next_student: I've got my lesson with Coach Arsenault right after this. I'm warming up my nerves.
I'm next. I'm not nervous. I'm a little nervous.
My lesson's at {until}. I'm watching the big girls do their axels so I can feel bad.
zamboni: I'm here to see the Zambelli. When does she come out? Is it now? Is it now?
I want to drive Doris when I'm big. Or now. Now is good.
Mom says the ice machine comes after. I'm waiting for it.
autograph: I'm hoping to catch {for} on the way out. Got a Sharpie and a clean card.
Waiting on {for}. They always sign if you ask nice and don't block the door.
fan: I just like watching. Better than television, and the fries are right there.
I come for {event} most weeks. Somebody has to sit in the stands.
Nobody in particular. I like a good skate. I like a bad one too, frankly.
drop_in: Just {doing}. It's warmer than the house and there's always something on.
I'm not here for anything. I'm just here. That's allowed, isn't it?
Came in for {doing}. Stayed for the gossip.
work: On shift till {until}. Then home and feet up.
Working. You'd know, you sign the cheques. Or you will.
Somebody has to keep this place running. Today it's me till {until}.
player: I'm out there at {start}. Just got to find my other skate.
Playing tonight. Wish me luck. Actually wish my legs luck.
Getting dressed. The room smells like 1994.
child: That's {for} out there. {they_cap} says {they}'s the fast one. {they_cap} is not the fast one.
I'm watching {for}. {they_cap} promised fries if {they} scored. I'm keeping score.
{for} plays. I come for the hot chocolate and to yell.
grandchild: I'm here to watch {for}. {they_cap} skated here when it was all outdoor. Apparently.

goal_mine: YES, {for_upper}! I filmed it! Did I film it? I didn't film it.
fall_mine: Oof. Get up, bud. You're fine.
fall: Everybody falls. Some of us twice a lap.
waiting: Come on, {for}. Some of us have work in the morning.
How long does it take to take off skates? Forty minutes. The answer is forty minutes.
{for}'s always last out of the room. Always.
I'll wait in the lobby. Tell {for} I'm by the trophy case.
zamboni: Look look look look look, the ice machine!
She's so slow. I love her.
arrive_car: Found a spot by the door. Miracle.
Somebody's parked across two stalls again.
arrive_foot: Walked over. It's cold enough to see your breath and that's just the lobby.
Ten minutes on foot. My ears are still on the sidewalk.
leave_together: There you are. Got everything? Both gloves? Both skates?
Finally. Come on, the car's warming up.

lines: Cold enough for you?
It's always cold enough. That's the whole building.
Ice looks {ice_word} today.
New owner's trying, I'll give them that.
You hear the Kings are thinking about a new goalie?
They've been thinking about a new goalie since 1996.
How's work?
Work's work. This is the good part of the week.
Did Doris start this morning?
Second try, I heard. That's a good day.
Fries any good tonight?
Lorraine's on, so yes.
They ever fix the heater over section C?
They fixed it in 2003. It's been retired since.
Is that the new owner?
Looks tired. That's how you know it's the owner.
Your shift change go through?
Had to promise Dougie my Saturday. Worth it.
You see Ronnie at the old-timers?
Still the best hands in the valley. Still the worst knees.
Snow's coming Thursday.
Snow's always coming Thursday.
Did you sign up for the 50/50?
Bud got me at the door. Bud always gets me at the door.
Who's got carpool Saturday?
Not me. Please not me. I did the 6 a.m. last week.
Did yours eat before?
A granola bar and a juice box. Dinner of champions.
Is that your kid with the purple laces?
Unfortunately. We lost a bet.
Coach moved Hazel to defence.
Defence builds character. That's what they said to me in 1991, anyway.
How much was the tournament fee this year?
Don't. I'm still recovering.
Whose turn is it for oranges?
Oranges? We're doing oranges again?
Mine wants to quit and take up figure skating.
Mine wants to quit figure skating and take up hockey. Let's just swap.
The test day's in three weeks.
She's landed the axel twice. Once on purpose.
He's taking forever.
He's doing his hair. For the walk to the car.
Are we getting fries after?
If he scores. If he doesn't, we're getting fries anyway.
Did you do the chem homework?
Define 'do.'
The vending machine ate my toonie again.
You have to kick it on the left. Everyone knows that.
Is that Dylan driving the Zambelli?
Earl lets him do one lap if nobody's looking.
My mom says I have to be home by nine.
It's 8:40. Run.
When's the ice machine coming?
After. It's always after.
I can skate backwards now.
Prove it. Also no you can't.
Do you have a toonie?
I have a quarter and a button.
I found a puck under the bleachers.
Finders keepers. That's the law.
Ice was better in '74.
Everything was better in '74. Except the knees.
Bev still sharpening by hand?
Says the machine doesn't love the blade.
You remember when the Cup came in '05?
I touched it. I'm not supposed to say that.
Gus would have had the lights on by now.
Gus would have had the lights on in 1987.
How's the hip?
Which one?
Busy tonight.
Busier than last week. Good for the place.
Hot chocolate's back on.
Finally. Civilisation.
Somebody left a glove on the bench.
There's always one glove. Never two.
